title: Deterministic Verification and a Single-Repair Guardrail for LLM‑Generated Network Configurations: a Paired, Shared‑Candidate Study
abstract: We report a sealed, preregistered paired experiment that measured the marginal verifier-detected effect of interposing a deterministic validator plus at most one automated repair on the same LLM-generated configuration candidate. Under preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation per intent reused for both episodes) we produced one candidate per natural-language intent with gpt-5-mini for N = 250 pairs and evaluated two episodes per intent: baseline (accept candidate) and guarded (deterministic_netops_validator_v5; if failing, permit one automated repair). Execution completed 500 episodes with model_calls_used = 251 (250 shared initial generations, 1 repair). Results: baseline verifier-pass 249/250 (99.6%), guarded verifier-pass 250/250 (100.0%); contingency n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = +0.4 percentage points, 95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp] (paired bootstrap percentile, 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729), exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. The single discordant pair was converted to pass by the single permitted repair. The preregistered sim‑to‑real/production-like contrast in the original plan was not executed; the confirmatory estimand reported here applies only to the synthetic/emulation partition actually run. All execution and analysis artifacts are archived in the study evidence bundle referenced in the Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are being explored as intent-to-configuration translators in network operations (NetOps), promising more concise operator interfaces and automated CLI synthesis. Stochastic generation, however, creates operational risk: syntax errors, incorrect command ordering, local-policy violations, and vendor-CLI subtleties can produce unsafe or nonfunctional device changes. Prior surveys and empirical work document that LLMs can produce useful draft configurations under controlled conditions while emphasizing the need for deterministic verification or human oversight [1],[2].

A common architectural response is the generate–verify–repair (GVR) pattern: accept only candidates that pass a deterministic validator and, when a validator-fail occurs, attempt bounded automated repairs targeting mechanically verifiable defects [3],[4]. GVR pipelines demonstrably reduce mechanically checkable error classes (syntax, ordering, simple policy violations), but important questions remain about the marginal benefit of inserting such guardrails when modern LLM outputs already match validator encodings for constrained tasks. In particular, when the same generated candidate is reused across guarded and unguarded conditions (shared_initial_candidate semantics), any observed difference must arise only from deterministic validation and repair rather than from differences in generation.

This paper presents a preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment designed to measure precisely that marginal verifier-and-single-repair effect under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Our contribution is a transparent, reproducible quantification (with uncertainty bounds) of the change in deterministic-verifier-confirmed intent-satisfaction when the identical LLM candidate is accepted versus when it is checked and allowed one automated repair.
sections.related_work:
Several streams motivate our design. First, NetOps-focused empirical studies and surveys demonstrate LLM feasibility for intent-to-configuration tasks in emulation and bench settings while noting error rates that motivate verification layers [1],[2],[5]. Second, deterministic verification tools and formal-analysis approaches (Batfish-style evolution, header-space/model-checking) are well-established for checking forwarding, reachability, and many local-policy properties and are widely recommended as validators in GVR pipelines [3],[6]. Third, generate-and-verify and program-repair workflows in code and configuration domains show improved detection/correction of mechanically checkable defects but do not fully solve deeper semantic or cross-vendor subtleties [4],[7]. Finally, security analyses of prompt-injection threats emphasize that filtering and validation are necessary defenses for LLM-integrated pipelines, particularly under retrieval or tool augmentation [8].

Our study differs from prior work in three ways: (i) it uses a preregistered paired design with shared_initial_candidate semantics to isolate only the validator/repair marginal effect on identical generated candidates, (ii) it reports complete provider-call accounting and deterministic reconciliation of generation and repair stages, and (iii) it archives validator traces and analysis artifacts so numeric outcomes are directly auditable against archived manifests.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study was preregistered (study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1; preregistration SHA-256: 7a984dbf7265...) as a confirmatory paired design with N_pairs = 250, generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate, and primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. The preregistration fixed the single-repair policy, exclusion/contamination rules, and the analysis procedures (exact McNemar two-sided and paired-bootstrap percentile CIs). The design permitted at most one automated repair per episode; independent first-pass generations per condition were not performed.

Task bank and constraints. A deterministic task generator created 250 constrained intent tasks (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5). Each task encoded initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and difficulty (medium/hard/very_hard). Payloads exercised realistic workflow constraints (e.g., make-before-break uplink switchover, paired-link atomic MTU changes, safe-service-transfer patterns) while limiting ambiguity to focus the confirmatory estimand on validator-and-repair effects.

Model and pipeline semantics. All initial generation calls used the declared model gpt-5-mini. For each intent exactly one shared initial-generation call was produced and reused for the paired baseline and guarded episodes. The guarded pipeline submitted the candidate to deterministic_netops_validator_v5, which implements full_intent_constraint_validation: CLI parsing, required_sequence ordering checks, workflow-constraint checks, and comparison of the validator-derived final_state snapshot to the expected_final_state from the task payload. If the validator returned valid = false in a guarded episode, a single template-driven automated repair (syntactic/order fixes only) was permitted and the repaired candidate was re-submitted to the validator. No iterative or human escalation steps were allowed by design.

Inclusion, contamination, and missingness rules. Pre-registered exclusion rules removed outputs that deterministically prevented verification (e.g., vendor-parser failures) or contained denylisted/credential-like artifacts. Contamination detectors flagged embedded instruction-like tokens or private-address artifacts. Per the preregistration, flagged items would be excluded from primary analysis; in this confirmatory run no episodes were excluded or flagged.

Analysis. The preregistered primary analysis used paired_binary_analysis_v1. We applied an exact two-sided McNemar test to the paired outcomes and computed a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the guarded − baseline paired difference with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). All analysis inputs and outputs are archived for audit.
sections.results:
Execution and reconciliation. Execution completed 500 episodes (250 pairs) with model_calls_used = 251: 250 shared initial-generation calls and one repair call. Provider-call accounting reconciles stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 250, "repair": 1} and hosted_model_call_event_count = 251.

Primary binary outcomes. Deterministic-validator-scored successes: baseline_success_count = 249 (baseline_success_rate = 0.996), guarded_success_count = 250 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). Paired contingency: n11 = 249 (both pass), n10 = 1 (guarded pass, baseline fail), n01 = 0 (baseline pass, guarded fail), n00 = 0 (both fail). The single discordant pair corresponds to the only exercised repair; repair-conversion rate on the confirmatory partition = 1/250 = 0.4%.

Statistical inference. Exact McNemar two-sided test on discordant counts (n10 = 1, n01 = 0) returned p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the guarded − baseline paired difference (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) is [0.0, 0.012] in absolute proportion units (i.e., 0 – 1.2 percentage points). These numeric artifacts are archived in the analysis outputs.

Representative validator diagnostics and repair. Validator traces for passed episodes show parsed_command_count matching required_command_count from the task payload (examples archived for inspection). Only one automated repair was invoked; its trace shows a deterministic reordering that resolved a required_sequence violation and produced a validator-pass on re-validation. No syntax-only or credential-contamination exclusions occurred in the confirmatory partition; contamination detectors reported zero flagged episodes.

Missingness, exclusions, and deviations. No confirmatory episodes were excluded: complete_pair_count = 250. There were no post-preregistration deviations that affected the primary estimand. The preregistered sim-to-real/production-like contrast in the broader plan was not executed; the confirmatory estimand reported here refers exclusively to the executed synthetic/emulation partition.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation of a near‑null marginal effect. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics and the constrained synthetic/emulation partition, the marginal verifier-detected benefit of deterministic validation plus a single automated repair was small: initial gpt-5-mini candidates satisfied the deterministic validator in 249/250 cases and the guarded pipeline converted the single failing candidate via the single permitted repair. The paired-bootstrap CI upper bound (1.2 percentage points) empirically bounds the possible verifier-improvement under these task and pipeline constraints.

Why the observed gain is small. Three artifact-grounded factors explain the limited observed improvement: (1) the deterministic task generator encoded constrained intents and allowed_touched_fields that reduced ambiguity and favored well-formed CLI sequences; (2) the declared model (gpt-5-mini) produced highly consistent, syntactically well-formed outputs for these constrained tasks; and (3) the deterministic validator measured mechanically verifiable properties (syntax, ordering, final_state snapshot) and did not attempt live protocol-level or cross-device emergent checks. These points are corroborated by the archived task manifest, raw responses, and validator traces.

Power, assumptions, and practical meaning. The preregistration power calculation assumed baseline pass rate ≈ 0.90 to detect a 15 percentage-point absolute effect with ≈80% power; the realized baseline pass rate (0.996) was far higher than anticipated. This departure reduces power to detect small absolute improvements and highlights that the observed paired-bootstrap CI, not a null-hypothesis rejection, is the most informative practical summary for this constrained setting.

Scope and operational implications. Our confirmatory evidence covers only the synthetic/emulation partition under constrained intents and a single-declared model and validator. It does not show that validators are unnecessary in broader or adversarial contexts. Validators that check additional behavioral invariants, multi-iteration repair policies, human escalation, diverse vendor encodings, or adversarial threat models could produce materially different operational benefits. Adaptive prompt-injection or retrieval-based attacks were not exercised here and remain open threats.

Reproducibility and auditability. All run artifacts—raw model outputs, task manifest, validator traces, repair traces, deterministic reconciliation, and analysis outputs—are archived in the study evidence bundle. Key numeric facts reported above (model_calls_used = 251; stage_counts: 250 shared initial generations, 1 repair; contingency counts n11=249/n10=1/n01=0/n00=0; bootstrap parameters) are reproducible from the archived manifests.
sections.conclusion: We executed a sealed, preregistered paired experiment under shared_initial_candidate semantics to measure the verifier-detected marginal benefit of deterministic validation plus one permitted automated repair on identical LLM-generated configuration candidates. In N = 250 constrained synthetic intent tasks, initial gpt-5-mini candidates passed the deterministic validator in 249/250 cases; the guarded pipeline converted the single failing candidate via the single permitted repair. Observed paired improvement = 0.4 percentage points (95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp]; p = 1.0). We emphasize that the preregistered sim‑to‑real confirmatory contrast was not executed and that the executed confirmatory estimand applies only to the synthetic/emulation partition run. Broader production, adversarial, multi-model, and multi-iteration repair evaluations remain necessary to establish generality. All execution and analysis manifests are archived in the study evidence bundle referenced below for audit and reproduction.

disclosure_statement:
Human role and autonomy boundary: After an autonomy lock required by the CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track, the autonomous system performed literature search, study selection, preregistration freeze, prompt preservation, model calls, deterministic validation, permitted repair execution, analysis, drafting, peer-review, revision, and finalization without manual human editing of technical content. A human Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and conducted pre-lock infrastructure development only; no human manually edited manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock.

Models, tools, and procedural summary: declared model = gpt-5-mini (provider recorded as openai_responses); deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; deterministic task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Execution used a guarded generate–verify–repair flow permitting at most one automated repair per episode as specified in the preregistration. Execution manifest reconciled model_calls_used = 251 (250 shared initial_generation + 1 repair) with stage_counts {"shared_initial_generation": 250, "repair": 1}.

Preregistration and immutable prompt reference: preregistration study id = study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1 (preregistration SHA-256: 7a984dbf7265c9a774eaf95c6c930dcf5f1e8845088bbc0e0855e3b4f1000ede). Immutable master prompt used to initiate the autonomous run: provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba. The full execution and analysis evidence bundle (task manifest, raw responses, validator traces, repair traces, deterministic reconciliation, and analysis artifacts) is archived and available as the study evidence bundle referenced by the preregistration identifier; those artifacts contain the per-file manifests and hashes required for machine verification.
limitations: Confirmatory scope limited to the synthetic/emulation partition; preregistered community and production-like partitions were not executed and remain exploratory.

Deterministic validator assessed mechanically verifiable properties (syntax, required_sequence, and final_state snapshot) but did not measure broader semantic or behavioral correctness (protocol dynamics, emergent interactions) in live devices.
Single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and one validator implementation were used; results do not establish multi-model or alternate-validator generality.
Only one automated repair attempt was permitted by design; multi-iteration repairs or human-in-the-loop escalation were not evaluated.
Adaptive adversarial and retrieval-based attacks (prompt injection, vendor-targeted exploit vectors) and large-scale production heterogeneity were not exercised and remain open threats.

The realized baseline pass-rate (0.996) departed substantially from the preregistered power assumption (~0.90), reducing statistical power to detect small absolute improvements; consequently, the paired-bootstrap CI reported here is the primary practical summary for this constrained setting.
